text.en: Sometimes a poet stretches a sound to fit the music of a line.

அளபெடை means the lengthening of a letter's sound beyond its usual duration (மாத்திரை) for the sake of rhythm in a verse. There are two kinds: உயிரளபெடை, the lengthening of a vowel, and ஒற்றளபெடை, the lengthening of a consonant (mei).
In உயிரளபெடை the long vowel is followed by a short vowel of the same kind, written in the line; it is of three types according to its purpose: இசை நிறைத்தல் (செய்யுளிசை), இன்னிசை and சொல்லிசை. These give the line its musical flow.
Practise spotting alapedai in verses, for example the extra vowel written after a long vowel in Thirukkural. Learn the terms எழுத்து, மாத்திரை, உயிர், ஒற்று and செய்யுள்.
